title: Israel elections: Netanyahu makes emergency call to voters, warns of high Arab turnout
content: Israelis are casting their votes in a crucial parliamentary election, testing the stability of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's administration. Impressively, voter turnout is the highest recorded at this stage since 1996, showcasing a keen interest among the populace. Gadi Eisenkot, leading the opposition, warns of potential ballot tampering that could affect electoral fairness.

title: Badoni joins Kohli, Gambhir in elite list with back-to-back double tons
content: In a remarkable display of skill, Ayush Badoni secured his second consecutive double century, remaining unbeaten at 210 in the Ranji Trophy against Jharkhand. Following his earlier 217 against Gujarat, he, along with Sumit Mathur, created a formidable partnership of 334 runs. With Delhi declaring at 515, they hold a significant advantage, while Jharkhand struggles on Day 2, finishing at 131 for four amidst a daunting deficit.

title: Swiss VPN company to re-interview staff on AI, and the results could decide who stays
content: Proton, the Swiss company behind Proton VPN and Proton Mail, will re-interview staff company-wide on how they use AI at work, with outcomes that could decide who keeps their job. CEO Andy Yen has assessed over 40 senior leaders. The AI interviews run from November 4 to 11, led by leaders from outside each employee's team, as part of a wider organisational review of talent.

title: Maine woman wins federal foreclosure fight over faulty $189,471 notice
content: In a landmark decision, a federal court upheld that Maine's foreclosure notification regulations extend protections to non-borrowing spouses. This case highlighted a scenario where a woman faced foreclosure due to her husband's refinancing actions, taken without her consent. The lender's notice was found lacking in clarity regarding amounts owed, underscoring the critical need for adherence to state laws which safeguard homeowners from improper foreclosure practices.

title: Is Jagan Reddy's 'regret' message a calculated alliance pitch for Congress?
content: YSRCP leader YS Jagan Mohan Reddy has publicly acknowledged his mistake of backing the BJP-led NDA government's law to appoint the CEC. Jagan, who was decimated in the 2024 assembly elections, is gearing up to navigate the complicated political landscape as the 2029 elections approach. Speculation abounds regarding a possible alliance with the Congress, creating formidable challenges, especially given the BJP's strong ties with Chandrababu Naidu.

title: Georgia man gets 15 years for $76m Ponzi scheme targeting 300 investors
content: Edwin Brant Frost IV, a businessman from Georgia, has received a 15-year prison sentence following his involvement in a Ponzi scheme that deceived more than 300 investors. This fraudulent operation caused a staggering loss of $76 million. Presenting himself as a reliable lender, Frost was actually battling significant financial turmoil. He misappropriated investors' money for his lavish lifestyle and political donations while neglecting loan repayments.

title: 'It was just me and Sooryavanshi': Abhishek after his record-breaking innings
content: Abhishek Sharma credited preparation and a clear game plan for his stunning 113 off 38 balls against New Zealand, saying he had “manifested” the innings. His partnership with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced a record 118-run powerplay, powering India to a six-wicket victory. Mentor Yuvraj Singh playfully challenged him to break his 12-ball T20I fifty record, while praising Abhishek’s explosive performance.

title: California adds 24,000 cubic yards of gravel to river; salmon spawn days later
content: A remarkable effort in California involved restoration crews who revitalized a section of the Lower Tuolumne River, focusing on creating vital salmon habitats and enriching local biodiversity. The project saw the introduction of over 24,000 cubic yards of gravel and 80 boulders, which collectively improved spawning conditions. Almost immediately after the work was completed, salmon flocked to the newly established habitats, showcasing the project's success.

title: Tirupati woman runs late husband's woodcarving business, supports 100 workers
content: After inheriting her husband’s woodcarving workshop, Chandrakala has skillfully transformed it into a thriving venture that generates more than Rs 1 crore annually and employs over 100 artisans. Her affiliation with the Lotus Self-Help Group has enabled her to tap into new markets, as she aspires to provide 500 rural women with sustainable job opportunities, showcasing the significant impact of women’s empowerment in rural entrepreneurship.

title: Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz says the ‘top job’ is not for him
content: Dustin Moskovitz co-founded Facebook and later started Asana, where he served as CEO for over a decade. Despite his achievements, he admitted that managing teams was not his true calling. Moskovitz faced increasing challenges during his tenure due to external social and political upheaval. Many corporate leaders, like Moskovitz, find themselves in management roles without formal training or desire. This phenomenon of the 'accidental manager' has become common in workplaces.

title: Why some children refuse group photos but happily take them, says psychology
content: Many kids feel uneasy during group photos, often opting out of the spotlight entirely. This discomfort could arise from feelings of shyness or anxiety in social setups, leaving them worried about judgment. Parents can ease this by allowing children to choose their roles in family events. Observing how kids react can offer valuable insights into their comfort levels with social interactions.

title: Watch: Houthis release dramatic drone strike footage from Saudi border regions
content: Recent footage unveiled by the Iran-aligned Houthis purports to showcase attacks on Saudi military sites at the borders. The group asserts it has specifically targeted Saudi forces in regions such as Najran, Jizan, and Asir, heightening regional tensions. Statements pointed to strikes on military transport planes and potential assaults on the Saudi defense ministry, intensifying security worries concerning the kingdom's military and crucial energy resources.

title: MIT students turn lunar waste into tools, win $925,000 in NASA competition
content: MIT students have pioneered a revolutionary recycling solution aimed at mitigating waste buildup on the Moon. As new supplies begin to arrive, it is vital to have efficient methods for dealing with packaging waste. This ambitious project, which has garnered accolades from NASA, seeks to transform waste into useful materials for lunar bases, setting a precedent for potential sustainability improvements both on the Moon and Earth.

title: Tom Brady’s referee criticism sparks questions: Are NFL owners limiting his role?
content: Tom Brady analyzed officiating decisions during a recent Packers-Lions game, focusing on controversial roughing calls against Green Bay. His dual role as a football analyst and Raiders part-owner complicates the situation when he questions referees. The NFL has established limits regarding his criticism to maintain official integrity and avoid excessive comments. No disciplinary actions have been taken against Brady, and his remarks have been within the acceptable framework so far.

title: Michael Olise’s parents: Who are Vincent and Mina Olise?
content: Michael Olise's decision to represent France at the 2026 FIFA World Cup is rooted in family as much as football. His father, Vincent, played cricket for Nigeria across nearly a decade and passed on a love of sport beyond the game. His mother, Mina, a French woman of Algerian descent, introduced Michael to chess and shaped his connection to France from childhood. Together, the two parents built a household where four nationalities, two languages, and multiple sports coexisted, producing a player who carries all of it with him.

title: California court upholds order to remove 19 trees after $78,500 settlement
content: In a protracted legal battle between neighboring homeowners in California, the Fourth District Court has decided that the invasive roots of 19 ficus trees must be completely removed. Although a prior financial settlement provided some relief, the roots continued to cause damage, prompting the affected homeowner to seek a more lasting remedy. The court ruled that total removal of the trees was essential to eliminate the persistent nuisance.

title: US midterms: Is Trump about to lose control of Congress? What betting markets say
content: Ahead of the November 3 US midterms, betting markets suggest Trump's Republicans could lose control of Congress, with Democrats favoured to win the House and Senate. The odds also point to a difficult contest for Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio.

title: Abhishek, Sooryavanshi set new world record in India's 3rd T20I
content: Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set a new T20I record for the highest run rate in a 100-plus opening stand, scoring at 18.13 runs per over against New Zealand. Abhishek smashed 113 off 38 balls, while 15-year-old Sooryavanshi made 45 off 18. Their 133-run stand powered India to a six-wicket win and an unassailable 3-0 series lead.

title: DJ Moore’s $5M mansion: Inside the 10,000-square-foot home listed after trade
content: DJ Moore’s North Carolina mansion remains unsold after several adjustments to its asking price. The Buffalo Bills wide receiver listed the waterfront property after being traded from the Chicago Bears to the Bills. The Charlotte estate boasts three levels of living space with several amenities like swimming pool, theater, gym, private balcony, and screened-in porch.

title: Connor Hellebuyck trade: How silence may have shaped the surprising deal
content: The departure of Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets stemmed from multiple pressures, notably concerns over salary and the potential for public conflict. In an effort to prevent any escalation, the team prioritized a trade, aiming for a swift resolution in consultation with team leaders. Internal tensions within the locker room further pushed management to act decisively, allowing the organization to redirect its focus to hockey without further distractions.

title: Man loses testicle after vasectomy; court upholds $9.5m malpractice verdict
content: A Pennsylvania appeals court confirmed a substantial medical malpractice judgment against Dr. Jason A. Smith following a vasectomy gone wrong. Matthew Brennen, the patient, experienced severe complications that resulted in the removal of his testicle. The jury awarded $9.5 million in damages, recognizing the pain and loss suffered by both Matthew and his wife, Lisa. The defense's arguments regarding testicular torsion were refuted by expert testimony during the trial.

title: Waited 3 months for silver Royal Enfield, got blue; dealer ordered to pay Rs 28,000
content: A Kerala consumer commission has taken a firm stand against a Royal Enfield dealer for unfair practices following a delayed motorcycle delivery. After an arduous wait of three months, the buyer received a different colored model, compounded by issues reported upon pickup. The ruling mandated the dealer to compensate the complainant with Rs 25,000 plus legal fees, with a strict 30-day timeline for compliance to avoid accruing additional interest.

title: Atlantic dye test shows 140 times more mixing within surface than across base
content: In a recent experiment near Martha’s Vineyard, scientists introduced rhodamine dye into the Atlantic Ocean to study its behavior. The dye spread quickly in the surface waters but demonstrated a slower descent into deeper layers. Findings showed a marked difference in mixing rates, emphasizing the complexities of ocean stratification on substance movement. This research is vital for the advancement of nutrient and pollutant transport models.

title: US court says detained migrants have no constitutional right to bond hearings
content: The US Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit has made a pivotal ruling concerning immigrant detention, involving three men who unlawfully entered the country. The court decided to overturn earlier decisions that allowed them individualized bond hearings while awaiting removal proceedings. This change stirs substantial dialogue on the potential impacts on the constitutional rights of immigrants facing detention without due process.

title: Gold prices have plunged: Should you buy yellow metal this Diwali?
content: If we look at gold from one Diwali to the next and it has rewarded patient buyers. On the MCX, gold has risen from Rs 50,986 per 10 gm in November 2020 to about Rs 1,45,800 now. That is almost 3 times the price. It has fallen in only one of the seven Diwali-to-Diwali periods (down 6.7% in 2021). The best run was last year, when it jumped 66.5%.

title: US assigns nuclear submarine to Australia under AUKUS as China expands Pacific footprint
content: The Pentagon has announced that the USS Colorado will be the first US Navy submarine in Australia's rotational force. This initiative aims to enhance military presence and deter China's naval influence in the Indo-Pacific region. The USS Colorado is scheduled to join Submarine Rotational Force-West at HMAS Stirling in 2027. The move is part of the trilateral AUKUS security partnership among Australia, the UK, and the US.

title: Diljit Dosanjh visits Taj Mahal as Delhi concert gets security clearance
content: Diljit Dosanjh made a noteworthy stop at the Taj Mahal during his Agra visit, admiring the stunning architecture while under heightened security. This excursion came just ahead of his eagerly awaited concert at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Delhi. After initial security hesitations from the Delhi Police, a successful dialogue led to the much-anticipated clearance for the event, part of Dosanjh's Aura India Tour on October 30.

title: Record alert! Abhishek overtakes Gayle after smashing 11 sixes vs NZ
content: In a stunning display of power hitting, Abhishek Sharma shattered Chris Gayle's record for the most T20I innings with 10 or more sixes. His explosive knock of 113 runs off just 38 balls propelled India to a smooth six-wicket triumph over New Zealand, achieving their target of 198 with 40 balls to spare.

title: Matvei Gridin’s Griddy celebration: Why did he dance after scoring twice?
content: Matvei Gridin scored twice for the Calgary Flames against the Toronto Maple Leafs and celebrated one goal with the Griddy dance. The prospect explained that the move connected to his nickname and felt natural because Calgary had built a three-goal lead. The moment added personality to his performance while drawing attention to the young forward’s developing NHL career.

title: Travis Kelce vs Patrick Mahomes: Inside their luxury homes and estates
content: Travis Kelce owns several properties across three states, spending roughly $12 million on his real estate portfolio. He purchased a Kansas City home in 2019, followed by a mansion in Leawood, Kansas, and a lakefront estate in Ohio. In contrast, Patrick Mahomes has concentrated his investments with a custom-built estate in Belton, Missouri, and a house in Texas.

title: The world's climate bill is mounting. But who should really foot the cost?
content: Developing nations are grappling with soaring costs from climate catastrophes, as seen recently in Nepal's pronounced losses. Commerce minister Piyush Goyal underscored the historical emissions from developed countries at a conference, urging wealthy nations to provide necessary support to those financially strained by disasters. Furthermore, the EU's new carbon regulations present additional hurdles for Indian manufacturers. Climate justice must involve an understanding of historical accountability alongside present capabilities.

title: Cyclone Arnab: All IndiGo flights from Vijayawada cancelled on October 28
content: In light of Cyclone Arnab, all scheduled IndiGo flights from Vijayawada Airport have been called off for October 28, with Fly91 and Air India also suspending various routes. Notably, flights linking Chennai and Bengaluru were cancelled on the previous day, October 27. Passengers are urged to verify their flight statuses prior to arriving at the airport, as ongoing adverse weather might trigger additional disruptions in travel plans.

title: Beyoncé's foundation gives $50,000 to nonprofit that says it helped 50,000
content: In a generous move, Beyoncé’s foundation, BeyGood, has granted $50,000 to In a Perfect World, which concentrates on youth empowerment. This financial support will help expand their educational and leadership initiatives, aiming to reach more young people in need. With its past achievements touching over 50,000 lives worldwide, the organization is crucial in filling the gaps left by funding shortages in schools, striving to uplift disadvantaged communities.

title: Meet Disha Daga, 26: Pune artist painted for RBI, taught 25,000 students
content: Disha Daga embarked on her mandala journey in 2016 as a creative pastime, transitioning to a professional artist. Garnering online recognition, she landed her first commission in August 2021, collaborating with esteemed clients such as the Reserve Bank of India. With a passion for education, Daga has hosted workshops for over 25,000 students, inspiring the next generation to embrace unconventional careers in the arts.

title: Watch: Serbia protesters storm pro-Vucic TV newsroom, capture editor
content: Live footage from Informer TV showed around 30 protesters entering the newsroom and gathering around Vucicevic. Some shouted, "This is how it is in free Serbia" and "Where is Vucic now?" while others called for the editor's arrest. Vucic, who previously served as information minister under former Serbian leader Slobodan Milosevic, maintained a strong grip on the country's media during his years in power.

content: India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for Andhra Pradesh as the cyclone is likely to cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam on Wednesday.

content: Saudi Arabia, the Middle East's largest economy, has suffered weeks of strikes from the Iran-backed Houthis against oil and civilian sites including Riyadh's international airport.

content: Operating EBITDA stood at Rs 401 crore, translating into a margin of 7 per cent, while EBITDA per tonne came in at Rs 414.

content: Sonia Gandhi said she was against her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, becoming the Prime Minister after the assassination of Indira Gandhi.

title: Delhi's Winter Pollution Curbs Are Back. Do They Actually Work?
content: Past episodes show that Delhi's AQI has often fallen after Stage IV of the plan was imposed. On 17 January 2026, the AQI stood at 400. It dropped to 192 within a week. In November 2023, it fell from 454 to 218 over the same period.

title: Stringent Criminal Law MCOCA Invoked Against Tiger Shroff Firing Suspects
content: A case against the accused was registered by the Mumbai Police on October 19 under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Arms Act.

content: The man, Daljit Singh, lived in Bhamme Kalan village. His family suspects that he died of a drug overdose. They allege that he went to Mansa on Tuesday morning to get drugs and was later found dead in fields near Ramanandi.

title: Congress Gets Permission For Ramlila Protest Rally. But There Are Conditions
content: The opposition alliance plans to hold its biggest rally against alleged "vote chori", or theft of votes, demanding accountability over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

content: The theft occurred around 4 pm when the businessman, identified as Champalal, stopped to eat a kachori and placed the bag containing the cash in front of his scooter when the two men took it and escaped.
